The 7 best trail running shoes of 2026, tested on 400 miles of mud, rock and snow

We ran in every shoe on this list for at least six weeks, on the same loops in the Peak District and the Cairngorms, and we weighed, measured and wore them out. Here is where we landed.

1. Kestrel Ridge 3 — Best overall. The Ridge 3 is the shoe we kept reaching for. The lugs bite on wet rock, the midsole is firm enough for long days and the upper drains fast. It is not cheap at £150, but it outlasted everything else here. If you buy one trail shoe this year, buy this one.

2. Norrbyn Fell Runner — Best for mud. Deeper lugs than the Kestrel and a narrower last. Brilliant on soft ground, skittish on road sections.

3. Altavia Pace — Best value. £85 and surprisingly capable, though the outsole wore through on the heel after 250 miles.

4. Tallow & Oak Summit — Most cushioned. Soft and comfortable, but we rolled an ankle twice on cambered paths.

5. Lumo Trailblade — Lightest. A race shoe, not a training shoe.

6. Ferrante Alp — Best for hiking. Heavy, stiff, indestructible.

7. Veltra Scree — The wild card. Odd lacing, great grip, poor sizing: order a half size up.

How we test: every shoe is worn by three testers of different weights and foot shapes. We buy the shoes ourselves and take no samples from brands. Some links on this page are affiliate links; if you buy through them we earn a small commission at no cost to you.

Pondmill recalls 40,000 kettles after reports of fires

By Hannah Reyes, 14 March

The appliance maker Pondmill has recalled about 40,000 of its Rapid 1.7 litre kettles sold since last September after at least eleven reports of the base overheating, three of which caused small kitchen fires. No injuries have been reported.

The company said on Thursday that a faulty batch of thermostats could fail to cut the power when the kettle boiled dry. Affected units carry batch codes beginning PM23 or PM24 on the underside. Owners are asked to stop using the kettle immediately and to request a free replacement or a refund through the company's website.

The product safety regulator said it was "satisfied with the speed of the recall" but would review whether the thermostat supplier's parts were used in other products. Pondmill's shares fell 6% on the news.

It is the second recall for the Leeds-based company in eighteen months. In 2024 it withdrew a toaster model over a similar fault, which consumer groups at the time said pointed to weak quality control. A Pondmill spokesperson said the two faults were unrelated and that the company had since changed suppliers.

How to set up a Norrbyn Mesh Wi-Fi system (and fix the three problems everyone hits)

I have installed a dozen of these for friends and family, so here is the short version of what works.

What you need: the Norrbyn app, the main unit plugged into your modem, and the satellite units unplugged for now.

1. Plug the main unit into your modem with the supplied cable and power it on. Wait for the light to pulse white, about two minutes.
2. Open the app, create an account and tap "Add network". Scan the QR code on the underside of the main unit.
3. Choose a network name and password. Keep the name under 20 characters; longer names confuse some smart plugs.
4. Once the main unit shows a solid light, plug in the first satellite in the room furthest from it that still gets a signal. Do not put it in the dead zone: a satellite needs a good signal itself to extend it.
5. Repeat for each satellite. The app shows the link quality as a bar; aim for at least two bars.

The three problems:
- Satellite stuck on amber: it is too far away. Move it one room closer, then move it back after it pairs.
- Devices dropping off: turn off "band steering" in Advanced settings. It fixes nine out of ten complaints.
- Slow speeds on the satellite: it is using the 2.4 GHz backhaul. Put it within line of sight of the main unit or use an Ethernet cable between them, which the system supports and nobody mentions.

If none of that helps, hold the reset pin for ten seconds and start again. It takes fifteen minutes and fixes most things.

Three days in Lisbon in February, which is the right time to go

Everyone told us February was a gamble and everyone was wrong. We had 16 degrees and sun on two of the three days, the streets were half empty and the pastel de nata queue at the famous place in Belém was four people long instead of forty.

Day one we walked. From our flat in Graça down through Alfama to the river, up the elevator at Santa Justa (worth it, go at nine before the tour groups), then lunch at a tiny place on Rua dos Correeiros where the owner's mother cooked and nobody spoke English, which was fine. Grilled sardines are out of season in winter; have the bacalhau à brás instead.

Day two was Sintra, and this is my one warning: take the 8.11 train. We took the 9.40 and the palace was already busy by the time we got up the hill. The Moorish castle walls were the highlight, not the painted palace, and we had them almost to ourselves because it started drizzling.

Day three we did nothing much, which is the point of Lisbon. Coffee in Príncipe Real, the botanical garden, a long lunch, a tram we didn't need to take. We flew home sunburnt. In February.

Quillon vs Notebird: which notes app should you actually use in 2026?

I have used both daily for over a year, Quillon for work and Notebird for everything else, so this is not a feature-list comparison copied from their websites.

Capture. Notebird wins. The quick-note widget, the share sheet and the voice memo transcription are all faster and more reliable. Quillon's share sheet still fails on long web pages.

Organisation. Quillon wins, by a lot. Nested folders, backlinks, a real search with filters. Notebird has tags and a search box, and that is it. Past a few hundred notes it falls apart.

Sync. Both fine. Quillon had one bad month in March when sync ate edits; it has been solid since.

Price. Notebird is free with a $4 a month tier for attachments. Quillon is $9 a month, no free tier, which is a lot for a notes app.

Verdict: Quillon is the better app if notes are a serious part of your work. Notebird is the better app for most people, and the one I recommend to friends who ask. If you want the capture of Notebird and the organisation of Quillon, you are out of luck; nobody has built that yet.

Ferrante Cycles opens its first North American factory in Portland, Oregon

PORTLAND, Oregon, 3 June — Ferrante Cycles, the Italian maker of steel and titanium bicycle frames, today announced the opening of its first manufacturing facility outside Europe. The 40,000 square foot factory in Portland's Central Eastside will build the company's Alp and Strada ranges for the North American market from this autumn, cutting delivery times for US customers from twelve weeks to three.

"Portland is the right home for us: a city that rides, a workforce that knows frames, and customers who have waited patiently for far too long," said Chiara Ferrante, chief executive. "This is the biggest investment in our 62-year history."

The facility will employ 85 people at full capacity and is powered entirely by renewable energy. Ferrante is also opening a flagship store and fitting studio on the same site, its first retail presence in the United States.

About Ferrante Cycles: founded in Bergamo in 1964, Ferrante builds handmade frames for road, gravel and touring. Its bicycles have been ridden to victory in three Grand Tours. Ferrante employs 310 people and sells in 41 countries.

Media contact: press@ferrantecycles.example

The safety bicycle

The safety bicycle is the design of bicycle that replaced the high-wheeler in the late 1880s and that remains the basic form of the bicycle today: two wheels of equal or near-equal size, a chain drive to the rear wheel, and a diamond-shaped frame with the rider seated between the wheels. The name contrasted it with the "ordinary" or penny-farthing, from which riders fell forward over the front wheel when it struck an obstacle.

John Kemp Starley's Rover of 1885 is usually credited as the first commercially successful safety bicycle, although chain-driven rear-wheel designs had been built by Harry Lawson and others in the preceding decade. The addition of the pneumatic tyre, patented by John Boyd Dunlop in 1888, removed the last advantage of the high-wheeler, its smoother ride, and the ordinary disappeared within a few years.

The diamond frame was refined rather than replaced during the twentieth century. Steel tubing dominated until the 1980s, when aluminium and then carbon fibre became common in sports bicycles; a number of builders, among them Ferrante in Italy and several British framebuilders, continued to work in steel and titanium. The geometry of the frame, in particular the angles of the head and seat tubes, determines the handling of the bicycle and varies with its intended use.

No-knead overnight focaccia

This is the recipe I make when people are coming over and I don't want to think. Ten minutes of work the night before, and the oven does the rest. This post contains affiliate links; I earn a small commission on purchases at no extra cost to you.

Ingredients (one 23 x 33 cm tray)
- 500 g strong white bread flour
- 10 g fine salt
- 4 g instant yeast
- 400 g lukewarm water
- 60 ml good olive oil (I use Tallow & Oak's early-harvest oil; any peppery oil works), plus more for the tray
- Flaky salt and rosemary to finish

Method
1. Mix the flour, salt and yeast in a large bowl. Add the water and stir with a spatula until there is no dry flour. It will be a shaggy, sticky mess. That is correct.
2. Cover and leave in the fridge for 12 to 18 hours.
3. Pour 2 tablespoons of oil into the tray. Tip the dough in, fold it over itself twice, turn it seam side down and leave it, covered, for 3 to 4 hours at room temperature until it fills the tray and is full of bubbles.
4. Heat the oven to 230°C. Oil your fingers and dimple the dough all the way to the bottom of the tray. Drizzle with the rest of the oil, scatter the salt and rosemary.
5. Bake for 25 to 28 minutes until deep golden. Let it cool in the tray for 10 minutes, then move it to a rack so the bottom stays crisp.

Keeps for two days wrapped in a tea towel. Reheat in a hot oven for five minutes.

Senior Backend Engineer, Payments — Lumo

London or remote (UK)  |  Full time  |  £95,000 to £120,000 plus equity

Lumo is a bank built for people whose income doesn't arrive on the 25th of the month. 1.4 million customers, 280 employees, profitable since 2024. What we are looking for

Apply with a CV and a short note about a system you are proud of. No cover letter needed.

Brightpath Help Centre › Cards

My card payment was declined. Why?

The most common reasons a Brightpath card payment is declined:

- Not enough money in the account. Check your balance in the app; pending transactions reduce the available balance before they appear in your statement.
- The card is frozen. You can freeze and unfreeze your card from the Card tab in the app.
- The payment was flagged as unusual. We may decline a payment that does not fit your normal spending, for example a first payment abroad. You will get a notification asking you to confirm it was you; confirm it and try again.
- Wrong details online. The expiry date, CVV or billing postcode did not match.
- Merchant restrictions. Gambling and cryptocurrency merchants are blocked by default; you can change this under Settings › Spending controls.

How do I see why a specific payment was declined?
Open the app, go to Payments, tap the declined payment and the reason is shown at the top.

What if none of these apply?
Message us in the app, 24 hours a day, and we will look at the specific payment. Please include the merchant name and the time of the attempt.

Kestrel Ridge 3 review: 300 miles in, and I want my money back

I wanted to love this shoe. Everyone on the running forums loves this shoe. At £150 it is the most I have ever paid for a trainer, and after 300 miles over four months I think it is the worst value shoe I have owned.

The grip is genuinely excellent, I will give it that. On wet rock and roots it is in a different class from my old Altavias. But the upper started to split at the flex point on both shoes at around 180 miles, which Kestrel's customer service told me was "wear and tear" and not covered. The midsole went flat long before that; by 200 miles the shoe felt like a slipper on a plank. And the sizing is off: a size 9 in these is tighter than a 9 in anything else I own, so my toenails went black on the first long descent.

For £150 I expect a shoe that lasts a season. This lasted half of one, and the company shrugged when I asked. If you want the grip, buy them and accept you will replace them in four months. If you want value, buy almost anything else.

Rating: 2 / 5

Suppressing dendrite growth in anode-free lithium metal cells through a dual-salt localised high-concentration electrolyte

Abstract. Anode-free lithium metal cells offer the highest theoretical energy density of any lithium-based architecture but suffer from rapid capacity fade caused by dendritic plating and the continuous consumption of electrolyte by the solid electrolyte interphase. We report a localised high-concentration electrolyte combining LiFSI and LiDFOB in a 1,2-dimethoxyethane/TTE mixture that yields dense, planar lithium deposits with a Coulombic efficiency of 99.6% over 400 cycles in Cu||NMC811 cells at 0.5C. Cryogenic electron microscopy shows an inorganic-rich interphase approximately 12 nm thick, dominated by LiF and B–O species, which we attribute to the preferential decomposition of DFOB⁻ at the plating potential. Pouch cells of 1.2 Ah retained 80% of their initial capacity after 220 cycles, against 61 cycles for a conventional carbonate electrolyte. We discuss the trade-off between ionic conductivity and interphase stability as a function of diluent fraction and propose design rules for diluent selection. Supplementary information, raw cycling data and the electrolyte preparation protocol are available in the repository linked below.

Keywords: lithium metal, anode-free, localised high-concentration electrolyte, solid electrolyte interphase, cryo-EM

Norrbyn senkt Preise für Mesh-Router um ein Viertel

Der schwedische Netzwerkhersteller Norrbyn hat die Preise für seine Mesh-WLAN-Systeme in Deutschland um bis zu 25 Prozent gesenkt. Das Einstiegsset mit zwei Stationen kostet ab sofort 149 statt 199 Euro, das Dreierset 219 statt 289 Euro. Als Grund nannte das Unternehmen niedrigere Produktionskosten und den Wettbewerbsdruck durch neue Anbieter aus Asien.

In Tests der Fachpresse hatte Norrbyn zuletzt gut abgeschnitten, vor allem bei der Reichweite und der Einrichtung per App. Kritik gab es an der Geschwindigkeit der Satelliten ohne Kabelanbindung. Ein Firmware-Update, das die Verbindung zwischen den Stationen verbessern soll, ist für den Sommer angekündigt.
